releasePlan.notes: Fresh string multivariate flag (control/v1), created dark; no prerequisite. Known limitation: LDClient.initialize uses a fixed context key 'anonymous-player', so every visitor lands in the same bucket and percentage rollouts or experiments split nothing. Randomizing by user is meaningless until a per-browser anonymous key is added. Also, v1 calls ldClient.identify() with the callsign as the context key: same-name players share a context, it adds LD MAU, and it re-evaluates every flag (including invaders-shooter-sprite) per callsign.

humanInput.question: The guarded-release metrics for enable-player-login (randomization unit 'user') cannot compare arms as the code stands: (1) LDClient.initialize uses the fixed key 'anonymous-player', so every visitor is ONE user context and a percentage rollout cannot split anyone; (2) on v1, identify({kind:'user', key:<callsign>}) replaces the user key mid-session, so post-login game-start/error events land on a context that never evaluated this flag (and can re-bucket the player). Proposed fix: (a) initialize with {kind:'user', anonymous:true} and NO key so the SDK generates and persists a per-browser key -- this is pre-existing code and ALSO changes how invaders-shooter-sprite is evaluated/targeted (any rule on key 'anonymous-player' stops matching, percentage rollouts start splitting) and raises client-side MAU from 1 to one per browser; (b) on login, identify with a multi-context {kind:'multi', user:<same anonymous user>, player:{key:<callsign>, name:<callsign>}} so the user key is stable and per-callsign targeting moves to the 'player' kind (v1-only new code). Reply 'approve a+b', 'approve b only' (metrics then stay monitoring-only until the shared key is fixed elsewhere), or 'neither' (all three metrics demoted to monitoring; release has no automated guardrail).
